correctness.rationale: The octahedral support function is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate divided by sqrt(2), so width is sqrt(2) times the maximum absolute coordinate of a uniform sphere point. Above the overlap threshold 1/sqrt(2), six equal coordinate caps are disjoint. Between 1/sqrt(3) and 1/sqrt(2), triple intersections have zero area and inclusion-exclusion has exactly twelve congruent pair lenses. The lens area is obtained by a spherical cosine-rule computation followed by sector-minus-triangle area. Endpoints and branch matching are exact. A packaged checker independently verifies normalization, direct spherical-area quadrature, and the lens integral.

originality.rationale: The closest older theorem gives all integer moments of regular-crosspolytope projection length through a Gaussian maximum and a high-dimensional limiting law, but does not give a finite n=3 CDF. A recent general three-dimensional polytope-density theorem applies abstractly but its explicitly evaluated models are the tetrahedron, truncated octahedron, and rhombic dodecahedron; its full text contains no crosspolytope occurrence. Finch treats tetrahedron and cube only. Searches under width, projection-length, caliper/Feret, maximum-coordinate, and exact-formula aliases did not locate the displayed octahedral CDF. The residual risk is that an older stereological or probability source records the same spherical maximum-coordinate law under different terminology.
residual_risks: Because the older all-moment theorem determines compactly supported laws uniquely, the accepted result should be understood as a new explicit evaluation rather than the first abstract characterization of the law.
An unindexed stereological source may use older terms such as caliper diameter or Feret diameter for the same directional-width law.
A probability source on the maximum of Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) coordinates could contain an equivalent formula without mentioning octahedra.

value.rationale: The regular octahedron is a canonical Platonic solid and the three-dimensional regular crosspolytope. Its complete directional-width distribution is a natural exact invariant in the literature's random-projection program and contains substantially more information than the previously emphasized mean and moments. The single transition at width 1 has a clear geometric meaning: it is exactly where pairwise overlaps among coordinate caps disappear. The resulting closed CDF is a useful benchmark for polyhedral density methods and maximum-coordinate probability calculations.
